text: New York's most creative night of the year. Tens of thousands of costumed marchers take over Sixth Avenue in Greenwich Village, with giant puppets, bands, and dancers. Free to watch, free to join in costume.
title: Village Halloween Parade

text: The famous Norway spruce arrives in Midtown and is raised by crane into Rockefeller Plaza on Meet the Tree Day, the unofficial start of the holiday season.
title: Rockefeller Center Tree Arrival

location: Central Park West to Herald Square
text: America's most famous parade: giant balloons, floats, and performances marching from the Upper West Side to Herald Square. Arrive early for a spot along Central Park West.
title: Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade

text: The switch is flipped on the world's most famous Christmas tree, topped with the Swarovski star, in a live televised ceremony with musical performances. Expect big crowds around the plaza.
title: Rockefeller Center Tree Lighting

text: Once lit, the tree glows daily from 5 AM to midnight through the holiday season, staying lit around the clock on Christmas Day. Free to visit, best on weekday mornings.
title: Rockefeller Center Christmas Tree
